clue.text: Ventures an Eastern greeting in a seaport capital

parts.note: to venture is to dare, so 'ventures' gives dares
salaam is the Arabic greeting meaning 'peace', used across the East

explanation.surface: Someone bravely offers an oriental salutation in a port city.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital is the Tanzanian port, long its seat of government.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the chief port of Tanzania and was formerly its capital city.

clue.text: A drink just before closing, perhaps

parts.note: a jar is British slang for a glass of beer

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks in one more drink at the pub just before last orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Closing' suggests pub closing time, but the definition describes a door almost shut; 'a jar' is British slang for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A door left slightly open is nearly shut, as if caught just before it closes.

clue.text: Jealous Casca was, according th to Antony in the play

definitions.text: Casca was, according th to Antony in the play

explanation.surface: A note on how a Shakespeare character described one of the conspirators.
explanation.walkthrough: In Julius Caesar, Mark Antony shows the crowd the cloak and says 'See what a rent the envious Casca made'; the stray 'th' is print debris.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean covetous: the plain synonym and the epithet Antony gives Casca in Shakespeare's speech.

clue.text: Boss finding dust all over the ne re place

indicators.note: something scattered all over the place is in disorder, so the letters are jumbled
this word means the letters it governs are mixed up, so they are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A manager discovers dust everywhere in the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' is the raised knob on a shield or ornament, not a manager; 'all over the place' rearranges DUST.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud and a boss are both raised ornamental knobs on a surface.

clue.text: Earl not represented could be in due course

indicators.note: re-presented, that is shown again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nobleman missing from a portrait might appear eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' signals that EARL and NOT are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean at some point afterwards, eventually.

clue.text: A river, no! Yes it is

definitions.text: A river, no! Yes it is

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: Someone denies a stream is a river, then is told it truly is one.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue builds A, R and NO, then insists the result really is a river: the Arno flows through Florence and Pisa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arno is the Italian waterway running through Florence.

clue.text: Talent of a part-time th copper?

definitions.text: Talent of a part-time th copper?

parts.words: Talent of a part-time th copper?
parts.note: a 'special' is a British volunteer constable, so a natural talent is pictured as that officer's present

explanation.surface: Wondering what aptitude a volunteer police officer brings.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a Special Constable, called a 'special', is an unpaid part-time officer; the phrase for an innate talent reads as that officer's gift. The stray 'th' is print debris.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural flair is often called a rare endowment or aptitude one is born with.

clue.text: Keen supporter jumping high over pillars in church?

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiastic follower
vaulting is leaping over a bar or obstacle

explanation.surface: An enthusiast is leaping about above the columns of a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the fanned stone ribs of a Gothic ceiling, which spring from the pillars.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a style of ribbed stone ceiling arching above the columns of late Gothic churches.

clue.text: An EEC monetary unit sounds straightforward enough

definitions.text: An EEC monetary unit sounds straightforward enough

parts.words: An EEC monetary unit sounds straightforward enough
parts.note: the currency's second word is said the same as an adjective meaning candid, so the coin sounds honest

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a European currency seems simple enough to understand.
explanation.walkthrough: The currency of France before the euro; its second word is pronounced like 'frank', meaning straightforward.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the money of France, an EEC member, before the euro replaced it.

clue.text: I'm more scantily dressed or inside Gilbert and Sullivan us coach

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the letters standing for the opera duo

parts.note: G and S is the usual shorthand for the comic-opera partnership
someone wearing fewer clothes could say 'I've less on'

explanation.surface: A performer complains of a skimpy costume in a light opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I've less on' (said by someone more scantily dressed) goes inside G and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To coach someone is to teach or tutor them.

clue.text: One who counts all the holes 01 too — except the nineteenth? re

definitions.text: One who counts all the holes 01 too — except the nineteenth?

parts.words: One who counts all the holes 01 too — except the nineteenth?
parts.note: a golfer tallying every tee, who avoids the 'nineteenth hole', the clubhouse bar

explanation.surface: A golfer keeps score on every hole but skips the clubhouse bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as TEE TOTALLER, someone adding up tees; the 'nineteenth hole' is golfers' slang for the clubhouse bar, which an abstainer shuns.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who never drinks alcohol would avoid the bar after a round of golf.

clue.text: Salmon for a king to knock back

indicators.note: to knock back is read as knocking the word backwards

parts.note: a rap is a sharp knock
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone is offered salmon in exchange for downing a king's drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RAP into PAR; then add R for king.
explanation.definitionFit: A parr is a young salmon in its first freshwater stage.

clue.text: Love is the key to a French department.

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: Romance is said to unlock a region of France.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oise is a département north of Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Oise is one of the administrative regions of France, named after its river.

clue.text: Outline study before round trip

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a tour is a journey that returns to its start

explanation.surface: Advice to sketch a plan and revise it before setting off on a circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A shape's profile or line around its edge is its silhouette.

clue.text: Three minutes in the ring le

parts.note: a boxing bout is divided into periods of three minutes each

explanation.surface: A short spell of fighting in a boxing contest.
explanation.definitionFit: In professional boxing each stage of the bout lasts three minutes.

clue.text: Most passionate after mixing the tots

indicators.note: the words are only used once stirred together, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Children are at their most excitable after a bout of mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: The most heated or fervent person shows the greatest fire.

clue.text: Socks a prophet booked in the OT

parts.note: hose is an old word for stockings or socks

explanation.surface: A biblical prophet is pictured wearing socks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'booked in the OT' means he has a book of the Old Testament named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosea is a minor prophet with his own book in the Old Testament.

clue.text: Old Athenian reformer and it's goodbye from him (almost)

indicators.note: almost the whole word is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: 'so long' is a casual farewell

explanation.surface: An ancient statesman bids farewell, nearly.
explanation.definitionFit: Solon was the lawgiver who reformed the constitution of ancient Athens.

clue.text: A timid follower unhealthily pale

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first, following it

parts.note: shy means timid

explanation.surface: A nervous hanger-on looks sickly white.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen or grey like cinders describes a sickly pallor.

clue.text: To come together is right and proper

explanation.surface: A note that gathering is fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to assemble; as an old adjective it means fitting or suitable.

clue.text: Great displeasure being out of range

indicators.note: the word is taken out of its usual order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is furious at being beyond reach.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong displeasure is wrath or rage.

clue.text: Complex new part on the Scheldt

indicators.note: complex means intricately tangled, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A new development is being built beside a Belgian river.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: the Belgian port stands on the Scheldt.
explanation.definitionFit: Antwerp is the major Belgian port city on the river Scheldt.

clue.text: Vice in a revolutionary scorned

indicators.note: one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: a red is a communist revolutionary
evil is wickedness or vice

explanation.surface: A radical is despised for his depravity.
explanation.definitionFit: Being reviled means being abused or despised.

clue.text: Adornment of flowers in pike country.

parts.note: the gar or garfish is a pike-like fish
a land is a country

explanation.surface: Floral decorations in a region known for its fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A wreath worn or hung as decoration is woven from blooms.

clue.text: … a hybrid rose heads gold-centred spray

indicators.note: the first piece goes at the head, in front of the second
a hybrid rose is a cross, so these letters are crossed into a new order
only the centre of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Gardener sprays a cross-bred rose whose flowers have golden middles.
explanation.walkthrough: ROSE is rearranged to EROS ('hybrid'); A plus that heads OL, the centre of 'gold'.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosol is a can that releases its contents as a fine mist.

clue.text: Pool giving pleasure to large number

parts.note: fun is enjoyment or pleasure
D is 500 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A shared kitty provides enjoyment for many people.
explanation.definitionFit: A pool of money is a shared reserve or kitty.

clue.text: Being a model for little Dorothy

explanation.surface: A small girl named Dorothy serves as a mannequin.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a model figure of a person, and the pet form of the name Dorothy.

clue.text: Proper centre for a swing

indicators.note: the middle letters, without the first and last, are taken

explanation.surface: Correct balance at the middle of a playground ride.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a cord hung from a branch serves as a swing.
explanation.definitionFit: A length of cord hung from a tree is a simple playground swing.

clue.text: Individual roundabout in times past

indicators.note: the first word goes round the next piece

parts.note: one is a single individual
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A lone figure went around in olden days.
explanation.definitionFit: Formerly, at one time, describes the past.

clue.text: Slow-moving creatures that S can fly

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift about into a new order

explanation.surface: Sluggish animals that still manage to take flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Owls are birds, animals that take to the air.

clue.text: Meet a blustering challenge at the brass band festival?

definitions.text: Meet a blustering challenge at the brass band festival?

parts.words: Meet a blustering challenge at the brass band festival?
parts.note: brass players arrive at a contest to puff into their instruments, while the phrase also means to start fighting

explanation.surface: Bands face a windy contest at a music festival.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for starting a fight is read as musicians turning up to play their horns.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin fighting physically is to start exchanging punches.

clue.text: Lapsed record brings back complaint

parts.note: to lapse is to slip, so lapsed means slipped
a disc is a gramophone record

explanation.surface: An old recording brings on an ailment of the spine.
explanation.definitionFit: A displaced spinal cartilage pad is a painful spinal ailment.
